checked: Sequencing and the distinction between written order and event order are defined before the methods. Time-signal words are explained with before/after pairs before examples use them.

Past perfect and past participle are introduced together and explained with regular and irregular forms before Example 2. Cause, effect, sanhi, bunga, and Filipino connectors are explained before Examples 5, 7, and 8. No unexplained units or symbols are required.

Core Concept explains how to reconstruct an event order that differs from written order. It demonstrates attaching before and after to their actions, interpreting past perfect, and using an explicit causal link.

Filipino instruction explains bago, matapos, pagkatapos, habang, dahil, kaya, and dahil dito. Worked examples show how those clues and named weekdays produce a reconstructed sequence. The lesson teaches its own sequencing goal without relying on unseen prerequisites.
The lesson states that meanwhile and habang do not determine starting order, before does not imply immediately before, and some orders can remain unstated.

Past perfect is described as a form that can show an earlier completed action, with surrounding text needed to identify the later action. Cause/effect teaching allows overlap and warns that an earlier event need not cause the next one. Strategies and Example 6 preserve these limits.
